m277E f_277E_010A copies the two-word/four-byte tail from source Voice tables; its callsites load instrument tables
src/data/d55B3_00B8.c defines nine six-byte instrument tables at offsets 0x0C42 + k*0x150, with pointer relocations to FMPatch/Sample resources

cross_tu_shared_object_view_chains.risk: This is stronger than a name-only collision: the registry and copy loop establish one six-byte DOS entry shape whose tail is pointer-bearing in the instrument-resource context. A native owner may use a tagged kind plus host pointer/reference union, but must translate the Voice raw-long/far-pointer source view. Do not preserve a far pointer as four opaque bytes when the native entries need real host references; preserve numeric 32-bit values only for modes with evidence that they are numeric.

m23AE and m2505 put flags at Win offset 0x1c and object pointer table at 0x2c
S26 Win inserts minWidth/minHeight at 0x18/0x1a, flags remains 0x1c, adds grid/zoom fields, and retains objs at 0x2c

Use offset-asserted DOS record views/accessors, not a host-native packed C object or an unreviewed single Win/Obj definition.

common_header_recommendations.contents: Use fixed-width signed/unsigned 8/16/32-bit value types. Replace bare int/unsigned only by reviewed source-member mapping. Keep C integer-promotion expressions visible; storage-width conversion does not settle operation-width semantics.
common_header_recommendations.basis: Historical MSC large-model code uses 16-bit int and 32-bit long; local native code already uses int16_t/uint16_t state and a SimDosEvent8 DTO.
common_header_recommendations.guard: No conversion-wide casts or blanket host-pointer typedef.

common_header_recommendations.contents: Canonical SimDosRect field order left,top,right,bottom is a strong shared layout candidate (38 identical source definitions); expose source-friendly aliases in per-TU compatibility headers. Keep XY and HV point views named separately, since Pt is defined in both orders.
common_header_recommendations.basis: 38 repeated Rect definitions all have identical field lists; 23 Pt definitions have x/y in 21 TUs and h/v in two TUs; Point typedefs include a v/h layout.
common_header_recommendations.guard: Verify fixed-width layout and rectangle edge conventions in the native build; do not infer Point/Pt semantic equivalence from two-word size.

common_header_recommendations.contents: Define a common raw 8-word event DTO plus distinct named views for byte-split modifiers, x/y-point aggregate, S11 compact event, and the S19 x6 field. Keep source member spelling/semantics in TU adapters.
common_header_recommendations.basis: 24 struct Event definitions produce seven field-list variants, including modifier byte split, Point aggregate, S11 short record, and S19 x6. Existing process_edit_event_dto.h demonstrates fixed int16_t event/rect DTO style.
common_header_recommendations.guard: Test offsetof/sizeof against witnessed DOS call records and preserve signedness; avoid generic Event alias.

common_header_recommendations.contents: Represent the shared window allocation as fixed-offset byte storage with named root/zoom views and checked accessors; provide separate object views for prefix geometry, type byte, and far-handle fields.
common_header_recommendations.basis: Window APIs join multiple TUs; root and S26 declarations preserve flags at 0x1c and pointer table at 0x2c while S26 adds fields. Obj views share type at 0x21 but not declaration shape.
common_header_recommendations.guard: No native pointer in the serialized/offset record; map far pointers/handles through explicit runtime references.

common_header_recommendations.contents: Separate fixed-width file wire DTOs (header, index row, record header) from OpenDB runtime state. Namespace the three source OpenDBRec and two IndexEntry declarations until each global offset is reviewed.
common_header_recommendations.basis: m1A28 reads/writes exact 14 bytes of DBHeader; m1986 reads 20-byte index header and count*8 rows; m19A9 reads ten bytes into DBRecordHeader from file offset+14. Shared fd_50F6_3958 table is declared with three nonidentical OpenDBRec views.
common_header_recommendations.guard: IndexEntry m1986 has a far data pointer where m19A9 reads a 32-bit offset; a native pointer is neither a stable wire field nor valid replacement.

common_header_recommendations.contents: Keep instrument, song and sample records namespaced by owning source role. A `SimDosSamplePrefix` may expose only the evidenced 14-byte shared prefix, with separate handle-token and sample-data accessors.
common_header_recommendations.basis: Instr has three incompatible layouts and is declared around same external name; Sample in m0000/m290D has cross-TU shared prefix, explicit pack(1) owner and direct calls. Song has three field layouts.
common_header_recommendations.guard: Retain DOS pointer indirection semantics; host pointers have different width. Do not merge Instr/Song based only on spelling/address-shaped identifier.

method: Parse frozen manifest-selected C files, strip comments, balance aggregate braces, and compare normalized member declaration lists and typedef base spellings. Report hand-audited shared-symbol/API chains separately. Counts are static and scoped; no AST preprocessing or compiler layout calculation.

single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.class: scalar byte maps and map-derived scalar state
single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.owner_rule: One owner per exact frozen storage address in SimGameWorld/source state; retain wider/shorter views as named accessors or aliases into that owner. Avoid bridge copies as an independently mutable second truth after calls return.
examples: MapA/LifeA are 128x64 byte maps; MapB/MapR/LifeB/LifeR are 64x64, PherMap arrays 64x32. portable/game/state/world.h already has corresponding arrays; session_bridge currently copies at the recovered-session boundary. Keep the established native world owner and make the copy an explicit boundary until zero-copy integration is proved.
These names are currently provided in the diagnostic catalog rather than missing contracts; do not count them as unresolved.
single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.view_model: Keep unsigned-byte map storage canonical. An omitted array bound is a view, not evidence for a second array. Exact-address aliases point to one owner slice. For mixed byte/word scalar views, preserve width, sign and endian through explicit accessors; avoid host union type-punning.
single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.limits: The catalog gives addresses/declaration views, not full extents, non-overlap or runtime sync proof; use accepted data layout and source differential.

single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.owner_rule: One native owner per actual source-selected object/table; use typed native references for real runtime pointers, explicit handle objects for Handle indirection, and tags to select views. Keep serialized source bytes separate from the native owner.
examples: fd_50F6_0000: 56 six-byte DOS entries; nine source data tables initialize pointer-bearing entries and f_277E_010A copies each entry. Native owner should be a tagged kind plus host reference union; translate Voice’s raw-long pointer path rather than allocating independent globals or copying four-byte far-pointer bits.
fd_50F6_3958: one database runtime table viewed as three OpenDBRec layouts; separate file wire headers/index rows from runtime names, handles and allocated index; expose reviewed field accessors.

fd_50F6_0150: sample free-list entries are far pointers (symbol registry gives 38 entries, four bytes each); native owner should be `SimSample *` or explicit reference IDs, not a copied DOS pointer table.
single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.view_model: Native pointers are correct for true host resource references (including local static asset pointers). Use fixed-width fields for DOS serialized bytes; use explicit reference translation for shared runtime objects whose source used far pointers/handles.
single_owner_native_global_recommendatio.limits: Do not infer that objects sharing an offset across overlays have identical lifetime; follow overlay/data ownership and initialization.
